limitations: Same fixed reachable-only cohorts as baseline; no new independent maps.
Node expansions are not runtime or energy. Budgeted means include capped failures; use ample-budget comparisons for completed searches.
Both rules retain f=g+h as the primary score; the alternative only changes equal-f ordering.
Tie-breaking is established, not a claimed new algorithm. Cohort-specific findings do not guarantee universal gains.

protocol.studentStatementVerbatim: 난 둘 다 똑같다고 봐. 내가 봤을 때는 여기까지 온 거리나 남은 예상 거리는 별로 중요치 않은 것 같아. 합계만 같으면 상관없는 것 같아.
protocol.studentPosition: The student considers the two equal-total candidates equivalent. He did not select the alternative rule or give a numerical prediction of node counts or success rates.
protocol.assistantOperationalization: Test whether changing only equal-f ordering changes node expansions and budgeted success while retaining optimal path length. This operational question is AI-formulated; do not attribute a quantified zero-effect hypothesis or the alternative implementation to the student.

variants.fifo: Smallest f=g+h first, then earliest insertion order; original default.
variants.closer-goal: Smallest f=g+h first; only at equal f prefer smaller h (equivalently larger g), then insertion order. Alternative proposed and implemented by AI.

protocol.controlledConditions: Reuse every accepted seed, density, grid size, endpoint and budget from the committed baseline matrix. Do not resample maps or change heuristic, movement costs, neighbor order, goal handling or closed-set rules. Replay Greedy only to verify unchanged baseline metrics.
plannedMetrics: Successes / 30 for each A* rule and every original density/budget condition.
Mean expanded nodes over all 30 rows, plus common-success counts and lengths.
Success gains and losses relative to FIFO, without dropping regressions.
Every successful A* path must be valid and equal the Dijkstra reference length.
Default A* and Greedy metrics must reproduce all 720 prior policy rows.
protocol.plannedDisplay: Report all 12 conditions. For the concise explanation use density .19/budget 120 success counts (same condition previously discussed) and density .19/budget 300 examined nodes when both complete; do not select the displayed condition after seeing the new outcomes.
protocol.knownPriorEvidence: Original FIFO matrix, student alternative eight-move route and previous teaching examples are already known. Small-map controls are planned tests, not blind discoveries. No full closer-goal matrix has been executed at protocol preparation.
protocol.attribution: Student statement is post-instruction qualitative reasoning. AI supplies the alternative rule, implementation, tests, comparison runner and execution. Tie-breaking is an established technique, not a claimed new algorithm. No hardware or runtime/energy result is claimed.
